title: bot.ability.reflection.input
description: Reflection input after the host handled a cognition result. Reflection recalls prior episodes, may select create/change/break, runs a change pass for create/change, marks break, and stores this turn; a failed or cancelled turn is only stored.

cognition_input.description: Original input payload given to cognition for this turn: its stimulus, focus and focus candidates. The original passes the live InputData (SkipJsonSchema); floppy passes it as data [floppy field].

stimulus.description: The event the body took for this turn, as an envelope: its name, its data, and optionally its id, source and target. The original passes the live stimulus object (SkipJsonSchema); floppy passes it as data [floppy field].

focus.description: Instance name the bot is looking at, if any.
focus.title: Focus

focus_candidates.description: Instance names that may become focus for this turn (body attention policy).
focus_candidates.title: Focus Candidates

cognition_input.title: Cognition Input

cognition_output.description: Typed cognition output selected for this turn and already handled by the host.

items.description: One selected modeled HSM event. Processing dispatches it to the resolved target fire-and-forget; hosts do not re-apply OutputData. Put selection rationale on reason here — not on the event payload.

examples.reason: Attention should move to that device for this turn.

anyOf.description: Stable reference used by a cognition host to resolve a target or modeled event.

target.description: Stable reference for the host-local receiver of the modeled event. Hosts may omit this when the event resolves relative to focus or a single actor.
target.title: Target

event.description: Canonical modeled HSM event name selected by cognition.
event.title: Event

data.description: Optional typed domain payload for the selected event. Trusted native abilities may retain a typed Pydantic payload through internal dispatch; model and learned-behavior JSON projections omit raw media. Do not put selection rationale here — use reason on this envelope.
data.title: Data

reason.description: Optional reason this event was selected.
examples: Attention should move to that device for this turn.
reason.title: Reason

items.title: EventData

cognition_output.title: Cognition Output

outcome.description: How the turn ended: completed (its output was sent), failed (the turn failed: failure says why) or cancelled. Reflection stores a failed or cancelled turn's episode with its outcome and failure and selects nothing for it (decision D139).
outcome.title: Outcome

failure.description: Why a failed turn failed, the message of the cognition's bot.ability.failed; null otherwise.
failure.title: Failure

turn.description: The body's processing turn this event belongs to, counted from 1 [floppy field].
